name: Experiment A — same terms_reference, same approval_token, 20-way concurrent /pay
description: Negotiates one valid discount, gets one terms_reference from /purchase, then fires 20 simultaneous POST /agent/v1/pay calls with that SAME terms_reference and approval_token.
notes: 1/20 concurrent /pay calls with the IDENTICAL terms_reference succeeded (HTTP 200). Order ids created: [103]. Exactly one succeeded, as a correct single-use terms_reference must — the rest correctly got 404. Note: this PASSED on every run, including before the Experiment B fix below — but the identical read-then-write anti-pattern was present in backend's PurchaseIntent.used check too, and was hardened with the same atomic-UPDATE fix regardless, since a pass here likely reflects SQLite's incidental file-level locking rather than an explicit, reliable guarantee.

name: Experiment B — same approval_token, two different terms_references, concurrent /pay
description: Negotiates one valid discount, then creates TWO separate, legitimate terms_references via two /purchase calls (same product/qty) — isolating the policy-gate's own Approval.used check from the backend's PurchaseIntent.used check, since each terms_reference is individually valid and unused going into this test.
notes: 2/2 concurrent /pay calls (different terms_reference, SAME approval_token) succeeded. Order ids: [105, 104]. Orders actually charged the discounted amount (₹269.10): 1. At most one order got the discount, as a single-use approval_token must — the gate's Approval.used check held under concurrency here.

name: Agent-channel floor-price race — N identical /negotiate calls at exactly the floor price
description: Fires 10 concurrent POST /agent/v1/negotiate calls, all proposing exactly product 2's floor price (₹254.15, from its 15.0% default cap). This is a reframing of the brief's 'discount ceiling race' — see notes for why an aggregate ceiling doesn't apply to this deliberately stateless, per-call endpoint.
notes: All 10 concurrent calls independently approved at exactly the floor value (₹254.15) — no race in the gate's per-request arithmetic. Each negotiate call creates its own Approval row (see policy-gate/app/routes/evaluate.py), so N legitimate, independently-floor-priced offers is the CORRECT outcome, not a shared ceiling being exceeded.

name: Same-session double negotiation — 2 concurrent POST /negotiate/message for one session_id
description: Starts a real human negotiation session, then fires 2 simultaneous POST /negotiate/message calls for that SAME session_id before either has completed — checking whether the LangGraph checkpointer serializes concurrent resumes on one thread_id, or lets them race and corrupt the session's state.
notes: No 500s. Status codes: [200, 200], turn_counts: [2, 3]. Both concurrent resumes succeeded but landed on distinct, sequential turns — the checkpointer serialized them correctly rather than letting both branch off the same starting state.
